France’s public healthcare ensures that pregnancy and postpartum care in state-run hospitals come at no cost. Working women can take a 16-week maternity break, receiving daily payments between €9.29 and €84.90, depending on prior earnings. Financially, having a baby doesn’t worsen existing struggles—low-income families face the same challenges as before, while those with means continue to manage comfortably.

Yet when it comes to actual support for new mothers, the system falls short. Fathers get just 11 days off, leaving mothers to handle recovery and constant newborn care alone. Finding childcare adds another hurdle, as government-backed options are scarce, particularly around Paris. Public daycare fees can be as low as €1,000 annually for lower-income families, but spots are limited—only one for every eight kids. Many turn to private solutions like nannies or in-home care instead.
